rundown: Eagles beat Harriers 104-69 at Ellis T. Johnson Arena in Morehead, KY in front of 1,032. Eagles led 48-30 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 99%).
Leading the way — Harriers: Sean Caldwell 23 pts, 5 reb; Marvin Good 5 ast. Eagles: Davion Cunningham 19 pts; Justin Payne 6 ast; Tayvion Tangiora 7 reb.
Where Eagles won it: they shot 55% to 39%, won the boards 51-24 and had 30 assists to 15.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 16, 10:55 AM ET. It had Harriers 60% and Eagles 40%, projecting Harriers 79.6 – Eagles 76.9 (156.4 total, Harriers by 2.7).

Final: Harriers 69 – Eagles 104. Wrong winner: it had Harriers at 60%, and Eagles (40%) won.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: MHAM pts scored, MHAM pts allowed, MHAM lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Harriers came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 79.6, they scored 69 (−10.6 points, 13% under); projected to allow 76.9, they allowed 104 (+27.1 points, 35% over).

Eagles came in with a 5% below average attack and a 6% leakier than average defense (2-2, 77 scored and 81.3 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 172 and 173 games of evidence. Projected to score 76.9, they scored 104 (+27.1 points, 35% over); projected to allow 79.6, they allowed 69 (−10.6 points, 13% under).

The bigger miss was Eagles' scoring (+27.1 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 173 against 156.4 projected (+16.6), about the 87th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Eagles by 35 against Harriers by 2.7 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (MHAM pts scored, MHAM pts allowed, MHAM lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.084 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +38.8 points. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 606 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.981 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Eagles attack ×1.040, defense ×0.985 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 37.7 points), no bet.
